descriptionHtml:
Case priority: P0 · stated in the UAT / ticket AC · UAT TC-07 step 5 + ER 5; TFA-92585 AC 5-7 · “Tasks can be sent to another app user in-app only, with the same delivery and record as Handoff”. Mixed: stated part — in-app send through the Handoff picker, sender/recipient/time record on both sides, recipient read-only, no email; our part — the sent list still present 35 h / 37 h after sending (Q7) (only the stated part makes a QA bug).

Approach · TC-07 Task Export · S16 Send the task list to a covering colleague in-app; both sides keep the record; recipient reads it, read-only

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U7 The task list can be sent to another signed-in app user (an NP or covering physician) in-app only, through the Handoff delivery (same recipient picker, same in-app delivery), never by email (UAT TC-07; TFA-92585 AC 5) — gate: blocked: TFA-92585 ready for pr; TFA-92586 ready for pr
  • U8 Each send leaves the same record as Handoff: sender, recipient and timestamp, persistent and retrievable on both sides (UAT TC-07; TFA-92585 AC 7) — gate: blocked: TFA-92585 ready for pr; TFA-92586 ready for pr
  • T2 The recipient opens the received list from their own account, read-only; the tasks do not become the recipient's own tasks (TFA-92585 AC 6; TFA-92585 How it works 4) — gate: blocked: TFA-92585 ready for pr; TFA-92586 ready for pr
  • U10 All of the above works in both Hospital and Nursing Home (UAT TC-07; UAT 3.3; TFA-92585 AC 12) — gate: blocked: TFA-92585 ready for pr
  • U9 'Email Tasks' is absent from the task screen: the button and the functionality, not just unused (UAT TC-07; TFA-92585 AC 11) — gate: blocked: TFA-92585 ready for pr

Test design technique: Happy path (happy-path) — Walk the normal flow exactly as the UAT / ticket words it; everything it names has to show up.

Given Sender with the S01 census (Hospital) and the S02 census (Nursing Home); a second signed-in @roundai.test account 'Dr. QA Covering <tag>' as recipient

When Sender: Task Export → Send → pick the recipient in the same picker as Handoff → send; open Handoffs → Sent. Recipient: Handoffs → Received → open the task list; open own Hospital and Nursing Home task views. Both contexts

Then Sender sees the send confirmed and a Sent record naming the recipient with a time; recipient sees a Received record naming the sender with a time, opens the same grouped list with no control to complete, edit or delete a task; the recipient's own lists and task views gain no patient or task of the sender's; no email step anywhere; …

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): U7, U8 (sender, recipient, timestamp on both sides), T2 (read-only, not the recipient's tasks), measured against the Handoff record in S18. Recipient-detail checkpoints mustContain the sender and all six seeded tasks of their census, groupedUnder for the pending tasks and attributedTo for the completed one (same as S01 / S02, Q5-neutral), and mustNotContain any task control (' …

Where it ran: local newspec-c (new Playwright specs); test method MULTI · Multi-device / multi-account; lane planned in the matrix: browser agent (blocked)

S16 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/TC-07.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Environment: local — main e02167f → 8b4be94a (10-20), local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane newspec-c.

Test method: MULTI · Multi-device / multi-account; secondary: AGENT · Browser agent — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on local; Source: newspec-c.
